newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX JGB futures break up, upside seen limited.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX JGB futures break up, upside seen limited.

text.p: Japanese government bond (JGB) futures maintained their upward momentum on Monday but dealers said the rise was likely to be capped before the lead contract came anywhere near a fresh record.
The market largely ignored a downward correction on the Nikkei with dealers saying there was unlikely to be any change in the current low rate policy.

"We're up a bit more today," said one dealer with a European bank. "There is a gradual realisation that they (the Japanese) are not going to put rates up for a while. So even if these levels are high, they aren't likely to fall much."
The lead March JGB contract broke back up through 126 to end at 126.08, 0.15 higher. Its previous contract high was 126.85.
The back months of the SIMEX Euroyen futures also inched higher with dealers saying the contracts were mainly following the lead set by the JGBs.
Euroyen spreads were actively traded in the absence of large directional changes.

"The June-September-December Butterfly was actively traded today with dealers looking for the spread between September and December to close in to the same spread as June/September," said another futures dealer.
He said they had been selling September and buying the other two months.

By 1115 GMT, the March 1998 Euroyen futures contract stood at 99.11, up 0.01 from its IMM close. The spread between June and September 1997 stayed unchanged at 0.07 while the September/December spread narrowed 0.01 to 0.09.
Eurodollar futures finished little changed in light dealings with some of the forward months slightly higher.
June Eurodollars ended at 94.39, down 0.01 from their IMM close on volume of 3,110 lots.
